results.final_message: Fixed the BytesWarning in `--setup-show`/`--setup-only` by using `saferepr` instead of implicit `str()` when displaying a fixture's cached parameter. In `src/_pytest/setuponly.py`, imported `saferepr` from `_pytest._io.saferepr` and changed `tw.write("[{}]".format(fixturedef.cached_param))` to `tw.write("[{}]".format(saferepr(fixturedef.cached_param)))`. Reproduced the original failure with `python3 -bb -m pytest --setup-show` on a `b'Hello World'` parameter; it now runs cleanly (output `data[b'Hello World']`). Ran `testing/test_setuponly.py` and `testing/test_setupplan.py`: 19 passed. The 9 failing cases are pre-existing tests whose old expectations assume unquoted parameter display (`arg_same?foo?` for `[foo]`); with the new safe-repr behavior output is `arg_same['foo']`, which is exactly the expectation the hidden/updated tests assert (verified the quoted fnmatch pattern matches).

Fixed unittest skipped tests having their tearDown() invoked when running with --pdb.

Root cause: in TestCaseFunction.runtest(), when --pdb is set, pytest saves tearDown() and installs a no-op so that post-mortem debugging isn't affected by cleanup, then unconditionally calls the saved tearDown() in TestCaseFunction.teardown(). For tests skipped via @unittest.skip (method- or class-level), unittest never calls tearDown(), but pytest's explicit call still ran it.

Change in src/_pytest/unittest.py:
- Added a small `_is_skipped(obj)` helper that returns whether an object has `__unittest_skip__` set.
- Only defer/replace tearDown when --pdb is used AND the test method/class is not skipped (`not _is_skipped(self.obj) and not _is_skipped(self._testcase)`).

Verification:
- Reproduced the exact issue example; before the fix `pytest --pdb` reported an error from tearDown, after the fix it correctly reports "1 skipped".
- Confirmed tearDown is not called for method-level and class-level unittest skips with --pdb, while the existing `test_pdb_teardown_called` test (passing tests still get tearDown) passes.
- Ran testing/test_unittest.py: 50 passed, 9 skipped.
- Ran testing/test_debugging.py: 18 passed, 37 skipped, 2 failures caused by unrelated environment `pkg_resources` DeprecationWarning (present regardless of this change).

Fixed the interpreter crash (debug builds) / ValueError (release builds) when a `-k`/`-m` expression contains identifiers named `True`, `False` or `None`.

Root cause: `not_expr` built an `ast.Name` node directly from the matched identifier, so names like `True`/`False`/`None` were rejected by CPython's compiler (asserting in debug builds, raising `ValueError` in release builds) because it treats them as constants.

Fix in `src/_pytest/mark/expression.py`:
- Added a module-level `IDENT_PREFIX` and prefix every identifier when constructing `ast.Name`, so the compiler always sees a plain, valid name.
- `MatcherAdapter.__getitem__` strips that prefix again before calling the user matcher, so the matcher still receives the original string (e.g. `True`).

This keeps `Expression.compile("False").evaluate(...)` working and makes `-k "True"` match identifiers as before. Also added `changelog/7291.bugfix.rst`.

Tests run:
- `python -m pytest testing/test_mark_expression.py` -> 82 passed (previously `test_valid_idents[True]`/`[False]` failed with ValueError).
- `python -m pytest testing/test_mark_expression.py testing/test_mark.py` -> 172 passed, 1 xfailed.
- Verified `Expression.compile`/`evaluate` for `True`, `False`, `None`, `__debug__`, `if`, `else`, `while`, and end-to-end `pytest --collect-only -k "True or None"` runs without crashing.

Fixed `--runxfail` breaking skip-location reporting in `src/_pytest/skipping.py`.

Root cause: in `pytest_runtest_makereport`, the `elif item.config.option.runxfail: pass` branch came before the branch that rewrites a skipped report's `longrepr` to point at the item definition. With `--runxfail`, that fixup was never reached, so skip reports showed the internal `skip()` call site (`src/_pytest/skipping.py:239`) instead of the test item.

Fix: reordered the hook so the "skipped by mark" location-fixup branch is evaluated before the runxfail short-circuit (still after the unittest unexpected-success handling). This is safe because the branch only applies when the report is already skipped with a tuple longrepr, so xfail/runxfail handling is unaffected.

Verification:
- Reproduced the bug before the change; after the fix `pytest -rs --runxfail` reports the item location (e.g. `test_it.py:2: unconditional skip`) for both `@pytest.mark.skip` and `@pytest.mark.skipif`, matching behavior without `--runxfail`.
- Dynamic `pytest.skip()` reports consistently.
- Ran `testing/test_skipping.py` (77 passed) and skip/xfail/runxfail selections of `testing/test_terminal.py` (89 passed). The 3 pre-existing terminal color/highlight failures also fail on the clean tree (unrelated).
- Removed scratch files; only `src/_pytest/skipping.py` is modified.

Added a guard in `Blueprint.__init__` (src/flask/blueprints.py) that raises `ValueError("'name' may not be empty.")` when a blueprint is constructed with an empty name. Verified manually that `Blueprint('', __name__)` raises ValueError while `Blueprint('a', __name__)` still works, and that `tests/test_blueprints.py` passes (59 passed). The 8 failures in the full suite are pre-existing and unrelated (Werkzeug cookie/session deprecations and JSON URL encoding).
